_what_this_is: The scientific content the dashboard renders: the question, the pre-registered predictions and their verdicts, the scale comparison against the source, and the cost. Kept here rather than in the HTML so that a number has exactly one home and the dashboard cannot drift from it.
_provenance_rule: Every number carries a `src` naming the file or record it was read from. A number whose source cannot be named does not go in this file.
question: Given the same loop, how far does it carry a smaller tower before it saturates, and what does the arm-by-arm record explain?

backbone.ours_note: 28 layers, all full attention, vocab 151,936, model_type qwen3
backbone.architecture_difference: The source's tower is Qwen3.5: hybrid linear:full attention at 3:1, multimodal, vocab 248,320. Ours is Qwen3: 28 full-attention layers, vocab 151,936. Our point therefore differs in architecture family as well as in size, which is the distinction this project exists to test — the source's own down-scaling (2B to 0.8B) held the family fixed.

items.claim: The 0.6B starting point scores below the source's 2B v1.0 on a held-out set, measured by our own code
items.evidence: zero-shot 0.4025 and after the v1.0 recipe 0.5775; their 2B v1.0 is 0.6525. Both our points sit below it.
items.cost: no new GPU time — both numbers were already measured for other reasons

items.claim: More arms clear the gate than the four releases the source needed (falsified if the plateau arrives in <= 4 accepted arms)
items.verdict: OPEN — the source's own scale trend predicts falsification
items.evidence: the gate is +0.020 on a 3-seed mean. Loop gain was +0.1400 at 2B and +0.0616 at 0.8B, so the leverage itself scales with the backbone; a log-linear extrapolation to 0.6B gives +0.0370, which is room for 1.8 arms. That is <= 4.
items.cost: this is the only claim that needs arms; one arm is 3 trainings under the source's design

items.claim: Arms that kept at 2B fail at 0.6B, and the reverse
items.verdict: SUPPORTED at 0.8B by the source's record
items.evidence: their 0.8B line's keeper "is a different recipe" from the one that kept at 2B.
items.cost: confirming it at 0.6B needs our own arm

items.claim: The bf16 scorer defect does not reproduce
items.evidence: our scorer's normaliser casts to fp32 before the multiply, so autocast(bf16) leaves a relative error of 5.8e-03 and does not change the argmax. Their seven failed experiments were their scorer, not the task.

items.claim: Position-collapse is the first failure mode to appear
items.evidence: the order gap closed rather than opened: canonical minus reversed was +3.10 pp zero-shot and -0.75 pp after arm 0. A readout collapsing onto option k would widen it. The source's own record agrees: order averaging at inference is null, +0.001.

predictions.tally: two confirmed, one not supported, one supported at a larger scale, one open — three of five resolved without a run

cost._what: Time and compute are this project's largest cost. Every figure here is read from a run's own artefacts, not estimated.
cost.currency_note: GPU-train seconds as recorded by each run's own meta.json

entries.bought: the v1.0 recipe's number at 0.6B: pooled top-1 0.5775 against a 0.4025 zero-shot anchor, one seed

anomaly._what: arm 0 against the source's own run of the same recipe
anomaly.note: 69x against a model 3.3x smaller. An H100 runs bf16 GEMMs at roughly 10-11x a 4070 and the model is 3.3x smaller, so hardware and size together explain about 3.3x. The GPU reports 100% utilisation throughout, which is not evidence of throughput: it means a kernel was resident during the sampling window, and a stream of small kernels reports 100% too. 4,496 tokens per step through a 0.6B model is ~1.6e13 FLOPs, so 41.8 s is ~390 GFLOPS, or 0.43% of the card's bf16 peak.
anomaly.hypothesis: fragmentation at the edge of VRAM. This project already recorded that at 94% of capacity the allocator thrashes and the same evaluation takes 61 minutes instead of 15.6; arm 0 peaked at 96%. Being tested by a 150-step run whose per-step seconds come from the heartbeat wrapper, against the same run under expandable_segments:True.

consequence.one_arm_note: 3 seeds, matching the source's gate design
